intake.what_is_missing: The list of the 25 new findings from the dashboard. It is not in the repository, not in docs/security, and no tool of this session reads the dashboard (the connectors that could reach the project's database were not used: the brief forbids connecting to it).
intake.how_to_give_it: Paste or save the export (any of: JSON array, CSV, plain text). One row per finding with at least: its id or title, the surface (function, table, page), the severity the dashboard gave.
intake.what_will_be_done_with_it: Each finding is matched to the registry below by surface (function name, table name) and by its first sentence; a match is a DUPLICATE (and counts once), a new one gets one of the seven statuses with its evidence. A finding is never marked resolved without a test, a catalog result or a live call that proves it.

proof_levels.local: a test of this repository passes against the real code with fakes
proof_levels.catalog: a read-only catalog query run by the owner returned the expected rows
proof_levels.live: a real call against production returned the expected answer

counts.scope: only the items listed in this file; the 25 dashboard findings, the 58 earlier alerts and phases 1-4 are not counted because their lists are not in the repository

proved.note: R-BUDGETS (durable budgets) is verified in the catalog but nothing calls it, so it is not counted as a fixed vulnerability

registry.surface: public.admin_set_profile_coords (anon could call it; body let auth.uid() IS NULL through)
registry.proof_level: catalog (owner's lot 0 query, 2026-11-01): anon cannot execute, the body requires an admin or the service role, search_path pinned
registry.notes: Seen in production: exec_anon false, exec_authenticated true, exec_service_role true, SECURITY DEFINER, search_path pg_catalog, public, pg_temp; the body refuses anyone who is neither service_role nor an admin and bounds the array at 1000. The HTTP answers (REST calls 1-2) were not seen.

registry.surface: public.projects INSERT policy (WITH CHECK auth.uid() IS NOT NULL) and created_by on UPDATE
registry.proof_level: catalog (owner's lot 0 and lot 0b queries, 2026-11-01): the INSERT forces created_by and the UPDATE of created_by is refused for a signed-in user
evidence: commit fd46ef688: REST calls 3-4 cover INSERT with a foreign created_by and the owner change after insertion
repo: set_project_created_by_trigger rewrites created_by on INSERT; trg_guard_project_created_by is BEFORE UPDATE OF created_by
registry.notes: Seen: INSERT policy WITH CHECK (auth.uid() = created_by) and no other INSERT or ALL policy; set_project_created_by() overwrites created_by with auth.uid(); guard_project_created_by() raises 'projects.created_by is immutable' when it changes and auth.uid() is not null; the only UPDATE policy needs ownership or project access. The HTTP answers (REST calls 3-4) were not seen.

registry.surface: destructive agent approvals: replay, retargeting, concurrent consumption, model-chosen tool, plan double execution
registry.notes: Consumption stays the compare-and-set on orch_actions / copilot_plans (no in-memory map). OPEN, see the three entries below.

registry.surface: approvals: no content fingerprint (a draft's text can change between approval and send); only named targets are bound
registry.notes: Needs the proposer to store a hash: a code change in the orchestrator, no schema.

registry.surface: approvals: handlers with no handler-level check (publish_credit, send_message, apply_to_gig, forget_memory, send_payment_link ...)
registry.notes: Their approval is enforced at the orchestrator only; caller-asserted markers remain by design.

registry.surface: a plan approved as a whole covers its destructive steps (delete_project, remove_collaborator)
evidence: src/components/agent/CopilotPlanCard.tsx sends one decision for the plan
registry.notes: Per-step confirmation needs a UI change and a product choice.

registry.surface: server-side fetch of a member-supplied address: extract-event-details, transcribe-voice-note, send-push-notification
registry.notes: DNS rebinding cannot be pinned from this runtime (stated, unchanged).

registry.surface: transcribe-voice-note let any member write a transcript into any message by id (and name any audio URL)
registry.notes: Found while fixing the SSRF; same function.

registry.surface: enrich-creator-profile / enrich-press-links / enrich-credits could be aimed at another member (and enrich-credits at everyone)
registry.notes: The platform batch (service role) had stopped working under the member perimeter; fixed in the same change.

registry.surface: send-invoice-email: unescaped HTML under our sender, any recipient, no volume limit, settled invoices flipped back to sent
send-outreach-draft: recipient and subject passed to the mail library as typed, unescaped body, no volume bound
invitations: invite-to-stage has no per-account volume bound; send-credit-invite no budget (project and event invitations were budgeted earlier)
registry.notes: Both go through send-transactional-email, which has its own caller policy.

registry.surface: campaigns: send-broadcast-email, send-waitlist-invite, process-scheduled-campaigns, process-drip-campaign
evidence: all four are behind requireAdminOrCron (supabase/functions/_shared/admin-guard.ts); content is admin-authored by design
registry.notes: Reviewed for authorization only, not for per-recipient volume. The dashboard finding is not known.

registry.surface: guest web search: cost bounded on the server before the provider; provider errors were echoed to anonymous callers
registry.notes: The durable quota is consume_public_presence_search (drizzle/migrations/0000), on the backend that hosts the function (Cloud). Fails closed where it is missing.

registry.surface: 16 handlers answered every request with a platform 500: a module-level response helper read a corsHeaders declared inside the handler
registry.notes: A regression of the CORS allow-list change, not a vulnerability; it is an availability failure of security-relevant functions (meetings, guest links, unsubscribe, bank).

registry.surface: desk-agent: the model's arguments could override _tool, so a find_user call could run add_collaborator without approval
registry.notes: desk-agent cannot be deployed to production (premiumSwitch.ts missing there): the hole stays open in production until it can.

registry.surface: seven database privacy alerts
registry.notes: The list is the dashboard's. One table (waitlist) has a stated contract and a lot; the others are blocked on decisions.

registry.surface: waitlist: a visitor can set the review state of their own row; no read/update/delete control in the repository
verification, subscription, badge and XP columns of profiles writable by their owner (repository carries the fix; production state unknown)
registry.notes: Production already denied members every listed column except four before lot C (preflight exposed_now); lot C leaves is_claimed, current_streak and daily_swipes unlocked because the app writes them. REST calls and a click-through of the profile editor, onboarding, daily check-in and undo swipe are owed.

registry.surface: profiles.phone_otp / phone_otp_expires_at / phone_number writable by the member: a self-chosen code verifies any number; the badge survives a number change
evidence: commit 0556f2cac: manual-sql/C_verification_badge (added to the lock list)
supabase/functions/_shared/phoneOtp.ts accepts a plain six-digit stored value
registry.notes: phone_number, phone_otp and phone_otp_expires_at were member-writable in production until lot C (preflight exposed_now), so a member could set their own SMS code; closed 2026-11-01 (03_verify: members can neither update nor insert them). REST calls not seen.

registry.surface: profiles columns members can write that look privileged: project_credits, invited_by, invite_code_used, referred_by_ambassador (preferred_currency is a display preference)
registry.notes: project_credits, invite_code_used and invited_by (writable) are now denied to members; available_invites already was; no function writes them. preferred_currency and referred_by_ambassador stay writable on purpose (the browser writes them); referred_by_ambassador only attributes the member's own row, the proper fix is to attribute at sign-up on the server.

registry.surface: browser writes members cannot make in production: profiles.current_streak (DailyCheckIn) and profiles.is_claimed (useProfileData and MatchedProfilesStep auto-provision)
registry.proof_level: catalog (lot0b: authenticated cannot update or insert either column) plus the code
registry.notes: Both flows answer permission denied today, before and after lot C. Fix: a server-side daily check-in function that computes the streak; drop is_claimed from the two upserts or provision the row on the server.

registry.surface: orch_approvals: a member can write an approval row (including a rejection) for another member's action id
registry.notes: Needs the target's action id (a uuid): hard to guess.

registry.surface: wallet top-up: claim, credit and revert are three statements (a crash leaves a paid top-up never credited)
registry.notes: Never credited twice (the claim is compare-and-set). The code change waits for the concurrency test.

registry.surface: no durable budget primitive on the production database (tables and functions absent)
registry.proof_level: catalog (owner's 03_verify, 16 of 16 true, 2026-11-01); concurrency and real-role behaviour not proved
registry.notes: Applied by the owner on 2026-11-01. The primitive exists in production; nothing calls it, so no protection is in force because of it. Wiring waits for 05_CONCURRENCY_TEST.md.

registry.surface: copilot_plans: a member may insert or update their own plan rows, steps included
registry.notes: copilot-executor now checks every step against the registry and refuses locked tools and foreign handlers; the row stays writable by its owner.

registry.surface: ThrivePromptHero sends audio_base64 to transcribe-voice-note, which has never accepted it (the home voice prompt answers 400)
registry.notes: A broken feature, not a vulnerability; needs a decision on the contract.

registry.notes: A first batch is prepared; nothing is extended to the 70.
